problem: Every result in this lane — C2, the d=2 replication, guided-first, and M2-P3's second-author replication — lives in ONE authored-world grammar: four primitives, builders of length <= 8, hidden chunks of length 2 or 3. The claim ladder names the limit in its own words: C3 needs a different grammar or a different acquisition mechanism. This study varies the GRAMMAR and holds everything else fixed.
what_varies_and_why_it_is_not_a_costume: Chunks become length 3 or 4 and chunk count becomes 10..16. This changes what chunking BUYS, not merely what it costs: builder lengths are sums of chunk lengths, so under a 3-4 band the attainable lengths are 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 — length 5 is UNREACHABLE — and the length-class structure the finding rests on is therefore different, not rescaled. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, recorded so it is not retried: a sibling substrate with more primitives (e.g. triple/halve, T 4->5) changes only the cost of enumeration; length-8 builders still factor into 2-3-op chunks. It also is NOT untried — m2p1/m2_ext_distance.py already ran a 6-primitive analogue (PRIMS6) and the d=2 law held on 6/6 seeds (D2_REGISTERED_GRAMMAR.md); what that analogue lacks is passage through the registered, gated, authored-world pipeline, which is what this study supplies.
why_chunk_count_moves_too: It is forced, not chosen. With t chunks of length 3 and f of length 4 the only tilings of a builder of length <= 8 are 4, 3+3, 3+4, 4+3 and 4+4, so members <= f + (t+f)^2 = f + k^2. At the M2-P2 cap of k <= 8 that is <= 72 against a viability floor of 90 members, and greedy search attains exactly 72, so the bound is tight and NO band-3-4 world can be viable at k <= 8. Clearing the floor requires k >= 10. Bound validated on 156 worlds, 0 violations (m2p4/BAND_FEASIBILITY.md, ledger row 61).

floors.measured_satisfiability: SATISFIABLE, but the viable region is concentrated at high chunk count and this is stated as a known constraint rather than discovered afterwards. Measured on the registered compiler (m2p4/records/BAND_K.json, 60 random worlds per cell): ZERO viable below k=13 — maximum members 77 (k=10), 84 (k=11), 89 (k=12) against a floor of 90 — then 3/60 at k=13, 2-4/60 at k=14, 6-8/60 at k=15 and 7-15/60 at k=16. The lane's own search nevertheless reached 6 viable worlds with 6 DISTINCT SHAPES in 62 random draws, so the worlds_min=6 and distinct_shapes_min=2 floors are jointly satisfiable; chunk count alone separates shapes (k=13,14,15,16 are four distinct shapes). An author who concentrates on k=10..12 will land CANNOT_CHECK_NO_VIABLE_WORLD; that is a measurement outcome and the bounds are NOT widened afterwards to rescue it. None of this is disclosed to the author unit — see forbidden.
